{"position": "Refactor in place this year, but spend a small fixed slice of that work on a decoupled write path so that a streaming rebuild becomes available later without a second one-way door.", "claims": [{"n": 1, "text": "A one-way door on storage format taken during a year with no roadmap slack is the specific combination that produces the worst outcomes, because the escape hatch and the schedule buffer are removed simultaneously."}, {"n": 2, "text": "In three-year-old ingestion pipelines, the dominant slowness is almost always a small number of identifiable hotspots — unpartitioned scans, per-record round trips, serialization, an unindexed join, missing compaction — rather than the batch paradigm itself, so profiling typically yields multiples of speedup for a fraction of a rebuild's cost."}, {"n": 3, "text": "Streaming architecture addresses latency, not throughput or cost, so if the complaint is \"slow\" in the sense of long job runtimes rather than \"stale\" in the sense of delayed freshness, a rebuild targets the wrong axis entirely."}, {"n": 4, "text": "The three years of accumulated correctness handling in the existing pipeline — late data, dedupe, replays, source-specific quirks — is undocumented business logic that a rebuild silently discards and must rediscover through production incidents."}, {"n": 5, "text": "The storage format decision can and should be decided separately from the batch-versus-streaming decision; coupling them is what makes the rebuild irreversible, and decoupling them costs far less than the rebuild does."}], "assumptions": ["The current pipeline is not at a hard architectural ceiling — i.e., no volume growth curve makes the batch design non-viable within roughly 18 months.", "The performance problem has not actually been profiled yet, or the profiling was superficial; teams that have measured usually already know whether refactoring suffices.", "\"No slack\" is a real constraint, not a negotiating posture, meaning a rebuild will be executed by a team simultaneously carrying feature commitments — historically the strongest predictor of half-migrated dual systems.", "Business requirements do not include a genuine sub-minute freshness SLA that batch cannot meet at any refactoring effort.", "The team has not already run a streaming system in production; if they have, my risk estimate for the rebuild is meaningfully too high."], "would_change_my_mind": ["Profiling shows the time is spread thinly across the whole pipeline with no hotspot above roughly 15 percent of runtime, indicating a structural rather than local problem.", "A committed product requirement exists for sub-minute or continuous freshness with a date attached, which refactoring cannot reach.", "Growth projections show the batch window colliding with the next batch's start inside 12–18 months, making the current design terminal rather than merely inefficient.", "The storage format is already forcing full rewrites on every run (e.g., no partitioning or no ability to append), meaning the format change is itself the performance fix and is unavoidable regardless.", "The existing pipeline has adequate test coverage and a spec-level description of its correctness behavior, which would remove most of the rediscovery risk I attribute to the rebuild.", "Leadership will actually grant slack — i.e., named features get cut from the roadmap in writing — which would invalidate my central objection about executing a rebuild under full feature load."], "confidence": 0.72, "nuance": "The hidden failure mode here is not choosing wrong, it's choosing the rebuild and then getting stuck at 70 percent for eighteen months running two pipelines and reconciling them, which is worse than either pure option."}
